engine_identity.title: Data-Driven Tower Defense Runtime
engine_identity.content_policy: Engine contains no named game world, entities, balance tables, level content, or user-facing copy. All such values arrive through GAME_DATA.

graph_model.nodes: stage IDs with unlock prerequisites and difficulty metadata
graph_model.edges: data references with optional mastery requirements
graph_model.curve_parameters: coefficient, exponent, midpoint, cap, step interval and seed are explicit data

progression.stage_model: Each stage is a sequence of micro_phases / encounters, not a static screen. Each micro-phase owns entry conditions, local rules, gameplay entities, route context, objective, spawn plan, decorative_layout and transition conditions.

density_metrics.validation: Rejects an under-dense generated stage with structured warnings and estimated active duration; estimates include spawn cadence, planning decisions, and objective beats, not idle pauses.

micro_phase_contract.entry_conditions: expression list evaluated by condition registry
micro_phase_contract.local_rules: rule IDs with scoped phase lifetime
micro_phase_contract.spawn_plan: entity archetype, count, interval, route, initial delay and per-group seed
micro_phase_contract.transition_conditions: all/any predicates on clear count, objective state, elapsed active time or explicit launch command
micro_phase_contract.phase_clear: all required groups spawned and all required active entities resolved plus objective gate

mid_stage_checkpointing.commit_points: phase clear before the next phase begins
mid_stage_checkpointing.recovery: On retry resume at the last committed micro_phase with saved resources / world state and reconstituted non-decorative entities; never reset to stage start.
mid_stage_checkpointing.integrity: schema-validated, checksummed, staged write with last-good recovery

layer_mapping_rules.foreground: LAYER_FOREGROUND; parallax 0 unless explicitly rendered as camera-relative foreground

progression.choices: Offer 1 of N data-defined choices at configured phase boundaries. A choice can grant a tower module, modifier, economy conversion, route-risk change, or objective tradeoff; cards expose cost, effect, and drawback before selection.
progression.tutorial: Read from progression.tutorial; keyed localization strings, ordered steps, expected abstract command/event, completion condition and recovery hint. No tutorial prose is embedded in engine code.
progression.meta_upgrades: Persistent, data-defined horizontal unlocks and mastery improvements with prerequisites, caps and spend sinks.
progression.decorative_layout_runtime: Read every micro-phase. Instantiate render-only records for every instance_count. Map background_far/mid/near to LAYER_BACKGROUND and foreground to LAYER_FOREGROUND; sort by z_index; apply parallax_factor to camera delta. Support row/col grid coordinates and row/col=null free x/y coordinates. Force has_collision=false and exclude records from ECS gameplay queries, RuleEngine, pathing, AI, placement and Arcade Physics.

rules.evaluation: Registered condition and effect handlers consume only data arguments; deterministic order, recursion budget and max-effect budget per fixed tick are enforced.
rules.safety: Unregistered types, invalid references, runaway trigger loops, and effect budget violations emit diagnostics and skip the invalid effect; critical corruption pauses play safely.

conditions.registry_contract: condition_id -> pure predicate(data, event, world, config)
conditions.decorative_guard: All built-in entity conditions reject presentation-only decorative records.

effects.registry_contract: effect_id -> bounded command handler(data, event, world, EventBus)
effects.atomicity: Resource and entity effects validate inputs before mutation; multi-effect rule outcomes are ordered and event traced.
effects.decorative_guard: SpawnEntity gameplay effects only create registered gameplay compositions; decorative_layout is loaded only by the presentation adapter.

modifier_system.formula: FINAL = clamp(softCap, hardCap, ((BASE + FLAT_SUM) * ADDITIVE_PERCENT_PRODUCT) * MULTIPLIER_PRODUCT * CONDITIONAL_PRODUCT * TEMPORARY_PRODUCT)
modifier_system.priority_model: Apply flat, additive percent, multiplier, conditional and temporary operations in declared stage order; priority sorts ties deterministically.
modifier_system.duration_model: Simulation seconds, phase lifetime, session lifetime, or persistent; expiration emits MODIFIER_EXPIRED.
modifier_system.diminishing_returns: Optional per-value soft cap curve with configurable threshold and exponent; hard caps applied last.

events.payload_contract: Plain JSON-safe object with event_id, timestamp, source_system, optional entity_id, and typed event fields.
events.delivery: Synchronous dispatch is limited to pure reactions; structural changes and event cascades are queued for next frame to prevent reentrancy.
events.diagnostics: Bounded ring buffer; debug UI can filter by category, severity and phase.

economy.resources: IDs and starting amounts are data-defined; no currency names or balance values in engine code.
economy.transaction_model: Atomic ledger entries with source, sink, amount, balance before/after, stage/phase and event ID.
economy.anti-exploit: Reward eligibility is event-derived, duplicate IDs are idempotent, and offline time never advances active combat.

runtime.renderer: Phaser 3 stable via pinned CDN script
runtime.physics: Arcade Physics adapter; only gameplay-layer entities receive bodies
runtime.logic_renderer_boundary: Plain JavaScript ECS owns simulation; Phaser is a presentation, input, tween, audio, camera, and Arcade body adapter.

factory_integration.integration_contract: A factory may inject one complete GAME_DATA object or package the mapped JSON files adjacent to this engine. Missing optional domains use typed defaults; missing required play domains show diagnostics and a recoverable data-loading screen.

genre_analysis.subgenre: lane-and-grid hybrid defense with branching upgrades and persistent mastery
genre_analysis.hybrid_structure: Discrete planning windows between continuous enemy waves; enemy routes, build cells, line-of-sight, tower roles, support coverage, resources, and phase modifiers form one tactical system.
genre_analysis.player_role: Defense architect responsible for a vulnerable objective.
genre_analysis.player_fantasy: Read the route, assemble a complementary defense, then adapt it as enemy pressure changes.
genre_analysis.primary_activity: Place, reposition, specialize, and activate defenses while waves traverse authored or generated routes.
primary_decisions: whether to accept risk for a stronger reward
genre_analysis.risk_model: Leaking enemies consume finite objective integrity; overspending creates future coverage gaps; counter-specific waves punish single-role builds.
genre_analysis.reward_model: Currency during a stage, phase rewards and explicit build choices, stage mastery, achievement progress, and persistent unlock currency.
genre_analysis.progression_model: In-run horizontal build choices plus persistent account unlocks and mastery records; content graph and curves are data-defined.
genre_analysis.replayability_model: Seeded route / wave variants, selectable difficulty and mutators, branching loadouts, challenge objectives, and score optimization.

reference_inspiration.method: Opened product/developer pages and checked feature descriptions; no names, art, characters, wording, or proprietary data are copied.

references.name: Bloons TD 6
references.design_lesson: Readable counters and meaningful upgrade specialization create build variety.

references.name: Kingdom Rush
references.design_lesson: Distinct enemy behaviors, terrain, and tactical active tools add decisions beyond placement.

references.name: Mindustry
verified: turrets require supplied ammo, coolant, or power
production and logistics interact with defense
references.design_lesson: Resource supply and support structures can make economy a spatial defense puzzle.

references.name: CrazyGames Tower Defense category
references.design_lesson: The runtime must boot quickly, communicate controls immediately, and remain legible at varied viewport sizes.

retention_drivers: counterplay that can be read before failure
short feedback loops inside a long stage
variation_pillars: enemy armor, speed, flight, shielding, stealth, and splitting tags

player_fantasy.controls: The player commands a portfolio of defenses and finite resources rather than directly steering a combat unit.
player_fantasy.long_term_goal: Clear a content graph at increasing mastery, unlock new strategic options, and beat seeded challenge records.

primary_loop: INPUT: inspect route, threat and economy
ACTION: place, sell, upgrade, retarget, activate, or launch a wave
SYSTEM RESPONSE: towers acquire targets and resolve attacks
CONSEQUENCE: enemies lose layers / defenses spend resources / objective may take leaks
FEEDBACK: range, projectiles, hit response, threat warnings and resource deltas
NEW_DECISION: patch a counter gap, save, or specialize
secondary_loops: Wave scouting -> identify counters -> adjust target priorities -> validate coverage
Tower specialization -> synergy coverage -> phase choice -> build identity
Economy investment -> delayed payoff -> survival risk -> future purchase capacity
Enemy split / shield / armor interaction -> target priority change -> area or support response
Leak event -> checkpoint result -> mastery adjustment -> replay
meta_loop: SESSION -> stage result -> XP / unlock currency -> unlock tower modules or mutators -> new loadout choices -> next session
endgame_loop: higher difficulty -> data-driven wave composition -> build optimization -> seeded score / mastery record -> challenge mutators

decision_density.expected_choice_points: at least one meaningful build, target, economy, or phase decision every 8-12 seconds during active play
decision_density.non_idle_requirement: Waves keep attacks and leaks reactive; phase transitions expose explicit build / launch choices and cannot be only wait-and-claim.

principles: gameplay data and runtime state are separate
registries extend content without type switch trees
system_architecture.direct_system_calls: Prohibited; systems publish or consume EventBus events. World/registry/adapter services are shared infrastructure, not system peers.

entity_component_model.entity_definition: Unique ID and set of component IDs only; no behavior, content type, or universal type field.
entity_component_model.composition_rules: Component values are plain serializable data. Runtime add/remove is supported. Archetype identity is a data bundle plus tags, never a class or entity.type.
entity_component_model.query_contract: Systems query required component sets; entity IDs remain numeric and component maps are indexed by ID.

micro_animation_system.implementation_rule: Phaser 3 Tweens mapped from entities.json fields; sprite sheets are not required for basic juice.
micro_animation_system.trigger_mechanism: Idle tween only on marked interactive / key entities; pointerover, pointerdown and destroy events drive hover, squash/flash and exit tweens.
micro_animation_system.destroy_policy: Tweak scale/tint/alpha then remove only the presentation object; ECS destruction remains event-owned.

fixed_loop.input_phase: Gather hardware events into abstract commands
fixed_loop.update_phase: Run ordered systems and JSON rules at fixed dt
fixed_loop.render_phase: Interpolate component snapshots into Phaser display objects

systems.purpose: Advance micro-phases, spawn schedules, wave states and authored decisions.
rules: phase entry and exit conditions are data-driven
systems.player_impact: Sets pacing and opens planning windows.

systems.purpose: Validate grid occupancy, cost, legal build zone, sell/refund and sequential upgrades.
rules: only gameplay cells are buildable; route cells and occupied cells reject
systems.player_impact: Turns spatial and economic intent into a legal defense build.

systems.purpose: Move active opposition along authored route segments and detect endpoint arrival.
rules: movement speed is modifier-evaluated; arrival is a gameplay event
systems.player_impact: Makes route coverage, slowing and leaks matter.

systems.purpose: Find legal targets by range, line-of-sight, tags and tower priority policy.
systems.player_impact: Makes targeting modes and placement geometry strategic.

systems.purpose: Resolve tower cooldowns and request projectile, beam, or area attacks.
rules: fire only when target remains valid and cooldown expires
modifiers: damage, rate, projectile speed, splash radius
systems.player_impact: Converts complementarity into visible combat response.

systems.purpose: Simulate pooled projectiles and apply hit/area/slow payloads through events.
rules: homing and straight travel are component strategies
effects: request damage and return object to pool
systems.player_impact: Makes attack timing and impact readable.

systems.purpose: Resolve armor, shield, resistances, layers, defeat rewards, split/spawn reactions and leak damage.
rules: damage type resolves against data-defined resistance and layers
systems.player_impact: Enforces counter coverage and rewards correct threat response.

systems.purpose: Track sources, sinks, conversions, capacity and scarcity for stage and meta resources.
rules: all transactions are atomic and ledgered

systems.purpose: Evaluate multi-condition goals, failure limits, chains and stage results.
systems.player_impact: Supplies varied win constraints beyond survival.

systems.purpose: Capture resumable stage state at phase boundaries and restore safely after failure.
effects: serialize position, resources, objectives, entities, RNG
systems.player_impact: Failure resumes at the latest cleared phase instead of erasing a long stage.

systems.purpose: Evaluate JSON conditions and apply registered JSON effects without content-specific code branches.
rules: priority desc, stable ID tie-break, bounded effects per tick
systems.player_impact: Enables new content mechanics through data when they fit registered primitives.

systems.purpose: Track event-driven mastery goals and grant persistent rewards.
rules: conditions use event counters, thresholds and tags
systems.player_impact: Makes mastery and alternate play styles persist across stages.

systems.purpose: Project immutable gameplay snapshots into ordered Phaser display layers and feedback channels.
effects: draw, tween, sound, particles, danger pulse
systems.player_impact: Communicates state, danger and rewards without changing simulation.

systems.purpose: Normalize hardware inputs into abstract gameplay commands.
rules: hardware identifiers never enter gameplay systems
systems.player_impact: Consistent controls across desktop and mobile.

systems.purpose: Evaluate data-defined transitions for pressure entities and phase states.
state: current state and entry time per entity
rules: priority order and one transition per entity per fixed tick
systems.player_impact: Distinct pressure archetypes use explicit behavior graphs.

systems.purpose: Expire and evaluate universal numeric modifiers.
rules: flat, percent, multiplier, condition, duration, caps
systems.player_impact: Shared tuning and synergies across towers, enemies, economy and objectives.

systems.purpose: Resolve gameplay-layer spatial overlaps; never examines background, foreground or UI records.
rules: decorative registry has no gameplay IDs or bodies
systems.player_impact: Allows content-defined blockers and contact mechanics without coupling renderer to rules.

system_dependencies.scheduling: Topological order with explicit phase and priority from core_architecture.system_order; event consumers observe queued events in the following event phase unless synchronous dispatch is declared.

matrix.data_flow: validated tower cost and transaction ID
matrix.gameplay_effect: coverage expands while future purchasing power falls
late-route enemies can become urgent targets
priority and range determine attack allocation
rate, speed and target movement influence hit probability

matrix.data_flow: impact, damage type, area and status payload
matrix.gameplay_effect: counter tags and area grouping create emergent efficiency
splash value competes with precision and leak risk
mutators alter economy and counter coverage without code branches

closed_loops: place -> spend -> attack -> defeat -> earn -> expand
scout -> counter -> target -> leak avoided -> mastery
phase clear -> choice -> modifier -> altered defense -> new threat response
emergent_chains: slow + clustered fast units + area attack -> high efficiency but weak coverage of shielded targets
armor + rapid small hits -> low throughput -> specialist damage choice gains value
support aura + range bonus + choke placement -> overlap-driven build optimization
leak threshold + optional high-reward phase -> risk/reward route choice

persistent_state: versioned user settings and progression save
state_model.separation_rule: Content definitions are immutable config; components are runtime state; save snapshots are explicit projections; Phaser objects and caches are disposable derived presentation.

entity_model.identity: Numeric runtime ID plus component membership only.
entity_model.archetypes: GAME_DATA.entities contains reusable component bundles; instances are composed at load/spawn time.
entity_model.runtime_composition: Add/remove components through World API; emit ENTITY_CREATED / ENTITY_DESTROYED; pooled presentation objects do not preserve gameplay identity.
entity_model.decorative_isolation: Decorative instances are presentation-only records in a separate registry and never receive gameplay ECS IDs, Collider, AI/FSM, or RuleSystem eligibility.

component_model.composition_validation: Unknown component IDs are diagnostics, not fatal exceptions; required component sets are checked against the declared entity archetype schema.

theme.texts: localization key map; values may be strings or plural forms
theme.font: font asset ID or CSS family

lore.type: data-only setting metadata; engine never branches on lore

entity_definition.localization_key: string refs only; no embedded display copy

game_data_schema.references: Every entity, asset, localization key, rule, modifier, objective, stage, phase and progression edge reference resolves or is reported with safe fallback.

rendering.architecture: GAMEPLAY STATE -> PRESENTATION SNAPSHOT -> Phaser Render Adapter. Render methods cannot change gameplay rules.
rendering.layer_rules: Collision and physics eligibility is restricted to LAYER_GAMEPLAY. Background and foreground layers cannot be reassigned to gameplay through data.

visual_coherence_protocol.strict_palette_locking: All palette-role-tagged assets resolve to theme.palette; invalid colors are diagnosed and mapped to a safe role fallback.
visual_coherence_protocol.grid_snapping: Gameplay buildable positions snap to one data-defined board grid.
visual_coherence_protocol.strict_layer_separation: Level data separates entities_in_zone from decorative_layout; no decorative records in gameplay lists.
visual_coherence_protocol.zero_logic_decorations: Anything loaded from decorative_layout is render-only and excluded from colliders, pathfinding, AI, Rule Engine, placement and ECS gameplay queries.

decorative_layout_support.coordinates: row/col grid placement OR row/col=null with normalized x/y free placement
decorative_layout_support.parallax: Apply camera delta times parallax_factor; clamp factor to 0..1
decorative_layout_support.collision: Force has_collision=false regardless of input; never create Arcade body
decorative_layout_support.logic: Separate presentation registry with no ECS gameplay identity; no rule/movement/AI/collision participation

audio.frequent_event_variants: At least two configured assets per frequent event; generated tone fallback uses deterministic choice and pitch jitter +/-5..10%.
audio.adaptive_music: At least two data-configured intensity states driven by threat density / objective integrity; crossfade without resetting playback position.
audio.critical_resource: When objective integrity or configured resource crosses its data-defined low threshold, emit a visual and audio warning with cooldown.
audio.asset_free_fallback: WebAudio oscillator/noise synthesized from technical envelopes; no copyrighted melody or hard-coded game sound identity.
audio.unlock: AudioContext starts/resumes only after user gesture; failures are diagnostics and never stop play.

assets.manifest: GAME_DATA.assets or data/asset_spec.json; image, sprite, icon, background, animation, audio, music, font, effect and particle types.
assets.loading: Preload screen tracks each asset and validates response; missing / malformed assets create typed placeholders and diagnostics.
assets.pooling: Reuse projectile and particle display objects; release audio voices, textures and tweens on scene/session shutdown.
assets.placeholders: Procedural Phaser Graphics / text silhouettes derived from palette role and entity components.

localization.fallback_language: Configured fallback locale, then key identifier with diagnostic.
localization.interpolation: Named parameters {value}; plural forms use locale category keys and count parameter.
localization.user_facing_copy: No user-facing content strings are hard-coded in engine. Technical identifiers and diagnostics may use stable codes.

save.storage: localStorage namespace from theme.save_key; optional platform cloud adapter may mirror.
save.schema: Versioned envelope {version, updated_at, checksum, settings, meta_state, checkpoint, last_good}.
save.serialization: Explicit JSON-safe projections for meta and stage ECS state; exclude Phaser objects, caches, transient diagnostics and derived target candidates.
save.migration: Ordered pure migration functions from older schema versions; unknown future version is preserved and recovery UI is shown.
save.autosave: After settings changes, phase checkpoint, achievement, result and unlock transaction; debounced write for non-critical telemetry.
save.manual_save: Menu and pause screens expose save action; checkpoint write is atomic from user perspective.
save.recovery: Validate schema, checksum and IDs; recover last_good or safe defaults; report corruption with reset/export controls.
save.checkpoint: Commit stage position, resources, objective state, tower builds/upgrades, alive opposition components, RNG state, modifiers and phase schedule at mid-stage boundaries.

offline_progress.background_accumulation: Only content-declared production components may accrue; elapsed time is timestamped, capped, validated and anti-clock-rollback bounded.
offline_progress.rewards: Offline rewards have a configured maximum duration and are delivered once through the normal reward pipeline.

targets.entity_scale: hundreds to low thousands of ECS entities with indexed queries and bounded per-frame work

performance.hot_path: No DOM reads, JSON clone, unbounded allocation or full registry scan in fixed update; queries use component indexes; event queues and diagnostics are bounded.
performance.pooling: Required for projectiles, impact particles, damage text and repeated short-lived wave entities.
performance.culling: Offscreen presentation objects are culled; gameplay simulation continues deterministically unless data configures an explicit sleeping policy.
performance.quality: Low / balanced / high effects modes alter particles, bloom-like accents and trails, never gameplay timing.
performance.lifecycle: Destroy scene-bound textures, sounds, tweens, event subscriptions and pooled objects on shutdown.

platform_adapter.fallback: Safe local adapter resolves unavailable ads as unavailable, score submissions as locally stored, and start/stop calls as no-ops with diagnostics.
platform_adapter.policy: No ad interrupts a critical combat action; reward grants require explicit successful adapter result.

validation.safe_defaults: Invalid optional data is replaced with typed defaults; invalid required play data blocks launch with visible diagnostics and retry / export routes.
validation.debug: URL ?debug=1 enables diagnostics panel, system timing, entity queries and event trace.
validation.failure_policy: Never fail silently; catch top-level runtime exceptions and transition to recoverable error overlay.

testing.test_harness: Built-in deterministic harness exposed through ?debug=1 and window.EngineTestHarness.
testing.synthetic_data: Test-only, theme-free GAME_DATA is generated at harness runtime, includes 4 opposition archetypes, 3 tools, 8 modifiers, 3 contexts and one phase with 3 decorative records using different render layers and parallax factors.
testing.quality_evidence: Each test reports TEST_ID, purpose, input, expected, actual, status and evidence in the debug panel and console; synthetic content is not bundled as shipped game content.
testing.traceability: DESIGN_ID -> spec entry -> runtime module / registry -> TEST_ID; index mapping is carried in this contract and the final response.

requirements: screen reader labels for DOM controls
danger expressed by icon / shape as well as color
accessibility.localization: Text expansion and right-to-left layout direction are data-driven; board remains centered while controls reflow.

engine_config_vs_game_data.separation: No theme, level, named entity, resource, enemy, tower, reward or balance constant appears in ENGINE_CONFIG or executable source.

quality_gates.pass_definition: All critical runtime harness tests pass; data validation is visible and recoverable; supported features match code; unsupported future content features are not claimed as implemented.
quality_gates.known_boundary: The engine is factory-ready but not a standalone authored game until external theme, entities, stage and progression GAME_DATA are supplied.

AI.model: Data-defined finite state machine; behavior logic uses registered transition conditions and effects, never boolean AI flags.

state_graph_schema.states: state ID -> duration, tags, allowed component effects
state_graph_schema.transitions: from, to, condition_id, priority, effect IDs

AI.archetype_behavior: Every opposing archetype declares its own FSM graph and tags; speed, shielding, flying, armor, stealth, splitting and support are expressed as components/tags/rules, not entity-type branches.
AI.built_in_runtime: Generic FSMSystem evaluates registered conditions and emits FSM_TRANSITIONED; route movement and attacks query state IDs.

simulation.model: Discrete-wave tactical simulation with continuous fixed-step route movement and attack resolution.
emergent_interactions: route coverage x tower range x target priority
enemy resistance x damage type x attack cadence
support radius x build position x modifiers
resource timing x phase rewards x future counter needs

procedural_generation.seed: Stored with stage and checkpoint for reproducible wave variants.
constraints: route connected from entry to exit
valid build cells exist across route coverage zones
each required counter has at least one legal answer
spawn budget fits phase density target
decorative references and palette roles resolve
procedural_generation.reproducibility: Same seed + content version + generator version yields the same generated topology and spawn schedule.
procedural_generation.validation: Generated layouts are validated before becoming active; invalid results fall back to last valid authored template and emit diagnostics.

difficulty.adaptation: Data-defined curve and optional performance band adjust future phases; never use HP multiplication as the only difficulty control.
difficulty.telemetry: Record attempts, leaks, build diversity, phase time and objective failures locally for transparent, opt-in adaptation.

rewards.anti-duplication: Event ID and reward ID idempotency keys prevent duplicate delivery after resume.
rewards.ad_reward: Only via platform adapter result; unavailable or failed ads grant no unearned reward and never block progression.

objectives.evaluation: Event-sourced progress is serializable and can resume mid-stage.

achievements.evaluation: Event-driven counters and state predicates; unlocks persist and emit ACHIEVEMENT_UNLOCKED.

replayability.content_swap: Different GAME_DATA sets alter routes, towers, art, language, objectives, economy and progression without changing engine logic.
replayability.theme_swap: Theme, lore, palette, assets and localized copy are external data only.

endgame.scaling: Data-defined stepped/logistic/soft-cap curves and pressure composition; no fixed named content in runtime.
endgame.record_scope: Local best score, fastest stage, fewest leaks, build diversity and challenge clears.

UI.model: GAME STATE -> PRESENTATION STATE -> UI; UI emits abstract commands, never mutates gameplay components directly.
UI.responsive: Phaser Scale.FIT equivalent, safe-area insets, pointer/touch and keyboard parity, board framing on resize.
UI.animation: HUD deltas tween from old to new values; menus and choice cards enter/exit smoothly; motion respects effects quality.

screens.purpose: Show progress, diagnostics and recovery actions.
Resolve manifest and generate accessible placeholders.
Continue, stage selection, mastery, settings and onboarding access.
Board, route, build palette, wave state, objective integrity, currency and threat feedback.
Freeze simulation, restore, settings, quit and save controls.
Present 1-of-N upgrade / risk / economy decisions at phase gates.
Summarize goals, leaks, rewards, mastery, achievements and next step.
Spend unlock currency, inspect progression graph and records.

onboarding.required: First seconds teach inspect route, place a defense, launch/advance a wave and read the primary objective.
onboarding.completion: Persist tutorial step and completion; do not block input beyond a data-defined guided step.

settings.persistence: Versioned local settings under theme.save_key namespace.

input.mapping: Hardware events are normalized by InputAdapter; systems consume commands via EventBus.
input.touch: Large hit targets, drag placement preview, pinch/zoom optional, no hover-only affordance.
